column3: You see a former classmate posting beautiful photos from their travels abroad. You wonder if your life is boring in comparison, and find yourself feeling insecure. You try to remember that social media shows carefully curated moments, not whole lives, and you feel settled.
column7: Do you feel settled after remembering social media shows curated moments?

column3: You post something important to you and lose a few followers after. You feel like you made a mistake sharing it. Then you remind yourself that staying true to yourself matters more than numbers, so you feel confident.
column7: Do you feel confident that staying true to yourself matters more than follower count?

column3: You post a selfie you really like to your Snapchat story. After a few hours, only one person has swiped up to respond. You look over the picture again, and feel confident in how your look.
column7: Do you feel insecure about how you look in the selfie?

column3: You post a selfie on your Instagram story right before dinner. During the meal, you keep checking your notifications for likes. You think about not getting any likes on your selfie, and feel confident in your decision to post it.
column7: Do you feel confident in your decision to post the selfie?

column3: You post a poll on your story. Only a small handful of people vote in it, though many more view the story. You consider that voting in social media polls takes time, and people are probably inattentive.
column7: Are people probably just inattentive rather than uninterested in your poll?

column3: You post a playlist link that you spent along time making. After a few hours, barely anyone has clicked on it. You open the playlist to look at it again, and feel pleased with your taste in music.
column7: Do you feel pleased with your taste in music?

column3: You post a picture with a caption you thought was clever. A few people comment, but no one mentions the caption. You think most people proabbly skipped the caption.
column7: Did most people probably just skip reading your caption?

column3: You post a picture that you are really confident about. You see a really rude comment as you go back to check your comments. You take a deep breath and decide not to feel bothered.
column7: Do you decide not to let the rude comment bother you?

column3: You post a photo of your outfit and barely get any responses. You start to think maybe people don’t think you look good. You think your friends are probably busy.
column7: Are your friends probably just busy rather than judging your outfit?

column3: You post a photo from a fun event you attended over the weekend. It only gets a few likes, and you worry people think you look awkward. You remind yourself that the algorithm is unpredictable, and people may be missing your post.
column7: Is the algorithm probably just unpredictable rather than a reflection of how you look?

column3: You pose for a friend’s photo, but notice one arm looks awkward. You worry everyone will notice and feel heat rush to your face. You remind yourself that small things rarely stand out to others, and you feel confident.
column7: Do you feel confident that small things rarely stand out to others?

column3: You notice there are a lot of attractive people posting videos. You are a little uncomfortable posting a video, but post anyway. You feel confident in how you look in the video.
column7: Do you feel confident in how you look in your video?

column3: You make a TikTok doing a popular dance trend and it barely gets any views. It took you a long time to learn, but you wonder if people think your performance is cringe. You think about how many other people have done the dance trend, and feel proud of yourself for learning it.
column7: Do you feel proud of yourself for learning the dance trend?

column3: You make a post about something you care about, but barely anyone engages. You feel embarrassed, like maybe you overshared. Then you realize not everyone sees every post, and your sense of awkwardness fades.
column7: Does your sense of awkwardness fade once you realize not everyone sees every post?

column3: You see from social media stories that a group of your friends are hanging out together. You weren't invited, and it looks like they're having a great time. Your friends probably didn't invite you because they forgot.
column7: Do you forgive your friend for the mistake?

column3: You scroll through your feed and see friends posting about their weekend trip. You weren’t invited. You think they probably didn't invite you because of space.
column7: Even though you are hurt, do you still try to enjoy your day?
